text:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected - streaming p99 spikes in region-us-west, impact: user streaming stalls, increased page faults :fire:

Maya (oncall): @here seeing p95 ~450ms, p99 ~2.3s on streaming endpoints. Alerts started 10m ago.

Maya (oncall): initial triage - suspect KV cache pressure; paging observed on nodes hosting kv-shards-3/4. Datadog shows sudden drop in hit rate and rise in page-in latency.

Alex (eng-sre): confirming logs - noticed high eviction rates and fragmented KV segments after a big traffic burst. Prefill window seems to be larger than decode window => mismatch.

Priya (runtime): grabbing runtime metrics now. If prefill is filling large contiguous KV regions it's causing decode threads to stall due to IO contention.

Ken (infra): paging info from node n12: /proc/vmstat shows increased pgmajfaults, dmesg has multiple "out-of-memory" killers? not killing processes but heavy swap activity.

Lina (CS): customers reporting streaming stalls during long responses, some session reconnects. Impacting 2 enterprise customers in us-west.

Alex (eng-sre): quick mitigation proposals:
- reduce prefill concurrency (runtime config)
- enable aggressive KV eviction policy for fragmented shards
- fallback to smaller model variant for streaming-heavy routes
- temporarily route traffic to other regions if capacity available

Maya (oncall): action plan: Priya reduce prefill concurrency to 1 for affected shard-group. Ken, start redirect of 20% traffic to us-east as fallback. Alex keep monitoring p99.

Priya (runtime): running command to drop prefill concurrency:
```bash
# runtime admin
curl -X POST "https://runtime-admin.internal/kv/prefill/config" -d '{"concurrency":1,"shard_selector":"kv-shard-group-3"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

Priya (runtime): config applied, prefill workers scaled down. Watching decode latency.

Alex (eng-sre): also bumping eviction aggressiveness for shard-group-3:
```text
eviction_policy: aggressive
max_fragmentation_ratio: 0.6
compact_interval_s: 60
```

Ken (infra): routing change initiated: 20% -> us-east via traffic-router v2. Will take ~30s to hit steady state.

datadog-bot: metric update: p99 streaming latency dropped from 2.3s to 1.2s within 90s of prefill scale-down :white_check_mark:

Maya (oncall): nice, still seeing some taily stalls intermittently. p99 ~900ms now. Keep an eye on streaming stalls counters.

Alex (eng-sre): digging into KV layout - fragmentation map shows many small live segments causing page thrash. Long-term we need a compaction job that prefers low-latency windows. For now running targeted defrag on shard-3 replicas.

Priya (runtime): starting targeted compaction (non-blocking) on shard-3 replicas. Command below:
```bash
runtimectl kv compact --shard kv-shard-3 --mode incremental
```

Maya (oncall): note: do not run full compaction during peak; incremental only. If compaction causes IO saturation revert.

Alex (eng-sre): logs from streaming worker:
```text
[stream-worker] decode_ms=12 prefill_ms=320 kv_pages_fetched=84 io_wait_ms=210 tail_stall=true
[stream-worker] decode_ms=13 prefill_ms=8 kv_pages_fetched=2 io_wait_ms=5 tail_stall=false
```
Observation: some workers see huge prefill_ms due to page-in. 

Priya (runtime): looks like imbalance: some requests trigger large prefill (long context) while decode for short contexts is fast. We need prefix-aware prefill throttles.

Lina (CS): customers asking for status. ETA for stable baseline?

Maya (oncall): With current mitigations (prefill concurrency=1, aggressive eviction, 20% routing shift) we expect reduction in 10-20 minutes. Will update.

Ken (infra): routing moved; health checks passing in us-east. No increased error rates observed.

datadog-bot: p95 streaming down to 260ms, p99 trending 720ms. swap_in_rate decreased by 70%.

Alex (eng-sre): running a quick probe to detect pages being read from disk vs memory:
```bash
ssh node-n12 'grep -E "pgmajfault|pswpin" /proc/vmstat | tail -n1'
# sample output: pgmajfault 3421 pswpin 12903
```

Maya (oncall): handoff: I'm on-call for another 30 minutes. If this regresses I'll stay, otherwise Alex will take lead for follow-up and long-term fixes. @Alex please accept handoff.

Alex (eng-sre): taking handoff. I'll coordinate follow-ups: implement prefix-aware prefill throttles, scheduled incremental compaction during low-traffic windows, and telemetry to detect fragmentation earlier. Will open a post-incident ticket with root cause notes.

Lina (CS): I'll ping the two impacted customers with an update and the mitigations we applied.

Maya (oncall): small follow-up: noticed one worker still showing IO wait spikes after compaction started. Priya can you pause compaction on that replica and escalate to infra if disk is overloaded?

Priya (runtime): paused incremental compaction on replica r4. Disk IO normalized.

deploy-bot: deploy event: rolling patch applied to runtime to add prefill concurrency control feature flag.

Alex (eng-sre): summary for the incident thread:
- Trigger: traffic burst caused high KV prefill activity -> fragmentation + paging
- Symptom: streaming p99 spikes and stalls, customer-visible reconnects
- Immediate mitigations: reduced prefill concurrency, aggressive eviction, route shift, targeted compaction pause
- Next steps: prefix-aware prefill throttles, compaction schedule, finer-grained telemetry, runbook update

Maya (oncall): closing active alert window for now, will monitor for next 60m. If anyone sees degradation reopen thread. :eyes:

Lina (CS): thanks team. I'll attach customer notes to the ticket.

Alex (eng-sre): creating postmortem ticket and assignments. Assigning to Priya (runtime) & Ken (infra) for follow-up work.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (severity: S2) - follow-ups created.
